newsitem.title: INDONESIA: OPINION - Indonesia: Time for a correction?.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Indonesia: Time for a correction?.

text.p: By Jos Parengkuan, Research Director
PT Lippo Securities, Jakarta

JAKARTA, March 27 - Jakarta has been the best performing market in the region in the last four months (25pct), outperforming Malaysia (+9pct), Singapore (+7pct), Thailand (-19pct), the Philippines (+13pct), Hong Kong (+8pct) and even the U.S. (+16pct).
An improved macroeconomic outlook, liquidity inflows, strong corporate earnings and attractive valuations have been the main contributors to the market surge.

On the macroeconomic front. the widening trade surplus, low inflation and declining interest rates have boosted investor confidence. Meanwhile, interest rates are expected to soften further on a three-month view, perhaps by another 50-100 bps before bottoming out, given the continued excess liquidity in the banking sector.
LIQUIDITY INFLOWS

Liquidity inflows have contributed significantly to the market's excellent performance. The weak Thai market and strong mutual fund inflows in the U.S. have prompted foreign investors to pour more money into this market.
What is interesting, however, is that this time around, we are also witnessing a strong flow of funds from domestic players, not just in the retail sector but also on the institutional side.
Based on data from the JSX, there were 24 domestic funds launched last year, raising slightly over US$1 billion. Of this, however, only approximately 12 percent is targeted for equity investments.

While the amount of domestic institutional money going into the equity market is still tiny at present, this appears to be the beginning of what we believe will be a rapidly changing structure of domestic investors.

There are at least seven more funds that are currently being processed for registration at Bapepam, and we believe there will be many more set up in the coming years as prospective investors gain a better understanding of stock investment.
POLITICAL TENSIONS
Against this rosy picture, however, we note that political tension is still unabated. Riots have erupted sporadically, prompted by mere rumours.
The recent ethnic violence in Kalimantan, the continued tension in East Timor, the attacks on churches and temples in Java -- all these incidences have contributed to the edginess in the air.
In the lead-up to the May parliamentary election, more outbreaks of violence are not to be ruled out, as disgruntled elements in the society take advantage of the situation to vent their unhappiness.
But in the larger scheme of things, we believe the upcoming election is essentially a non-event for two reasons.
First, the result is pretty much known: a Golkar victory is assured, and in all likelihood, with more votes than that secured in the last election.

Second, this year's election affects only the parliament and not the presidency. The presidential election is not until March 1998, and thus, no changes to the government nor to major economic policies are expected this year.
SUSTAINABLE RALLY
So, the reality is that this market has all the ingredients for a sustainable rally. However, reality and perception often differ, and unfortunately, the former quite often succumbs to the latter.
Today. concerns about a potential market correction in the second quarter have prompted some investors to get reay to re-position their holdings.
Although the recent riots have not rattled the market, everyone is watching the political situation closely.

Interestingly, most investors agree that Indonesia will have a smooth election in May. Nevertheless, with investors having earned handsome returns on their investments in the last four months and the perception that others might take a more cautious stance ahead of the elections, the concern could well become self-fulfilling and lead to a market correction.
This, we believe, could materialise in the latter part of March or the beginning of April, although we do not expect to see a hard landing.

Given the market's apparent vulnerability to a correction, we feel it is essential that investors focus on counters that are expected to produce strong earnings in the upcoming reporting season and are still trading at undemanding PE multiples.
Banking remains our favoured sector at this time, considering the likelihood of a further margin expansion and the strong loan book registered by most of the listed banks in 4Q96.

However, with the recent rally in most of the big-cap counters, the choice is becoming somewhat limited. Our top pick in the sector is BDNI, which we rate as one of the most attractive bank counters in terms of valuation, growth outlook, share liquidity and potential earnings surprises combined.
Modern Bank is grossly undervalued at 6xFY97 EPS, a whopping 54 percent discount to the sector's rating of 13.1x.
OUTSIDE THE BANKING SECTOR
Outside banking, we like Mulia Industrindo which reported a strong margin expansion in 4Q96, a trend which we expect to continue in the upcoming quarters.
With all the bad news already reflected in the share price and the likelihood that float glass prices will be raised in the near term, the counter looks set to outperform.

In the pharmaceutical sector, Temp Scan looks attractive with its acquisition of Supra Usadhatama likely to be priced favourably. Moreover, there is talk in the market that a prominent professional is about to join the management team.
Darya Varia also looks interesting. Its FY96 result is likely to exceed the market's expectation, and the counter is trading at the low end of its historic valuation range.

Sampoerna's share price rose 2.3 percent on Wednesday on the back of speculation that the company may announce an acquisition of another cigarette company and/or increase its stake in its distribution company at a meeting with analysts on Thursday. At 24x FY97 earnings, the counter's valuation is not excessive.
(NOTE-The views expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as reflecting the views of Reuters).
